title: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB vs Intenso Premium Line 64 GB

brand.product: SanDisk Ultra USB-Stick, 64 GB, USB-A 3.2 Gen 1

key_ingredients.name: Read and write speed
key_ingredients.amount: read up to 130 MB/s, write up to 95 MB/s

alternative.product: Intenso Premium Line USB-Stick, 64 GB, USB-A 3.2 Gen 1

summary: Both are 64 GB USB-A sticks on the 5 Gbit/s USB 3.2 Gen 1 standard, and Intenso costs about 24% less at alternate.
evidence: alternate.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, including VAT, both available immediately and with no crossed-out price: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB EUR 15.69, Intenso Premium Line 64 GB EUR 11.99. Both list USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 at 5 Gbit/s.
differences: SanDisk states read up to 130 MB/s and write up to 95 MB/s, and includes SanDisk SecureAccess encryption software. Alternate's page gives no speed for the Intenso, so it may be slower, especially at writing. Intenso has a metal body and is smaller, at 32 x 5 x 12 mm. Warranty isn't listed for either on these pages. Shipping starts at EUR 7.99, so this pays when added to a bigger order. No test we read covers these two.
why: For moving documents and photos now and then, the capacity and connection are the same. If you copy big files often, the SanDisk's stated speed may be worth the difference.

title: SanDisk Ultra USB Type-C 128 GB vs ADATA UC300 128 GB

brand.product: SanDisk Ultra USB Type-C USB-Stick, 128 GB

summary: Both are 128 GB USB-C sticks on the USB 3.2 Gen 1 standard, and ADATA costs about 29% less, with a lower stated read speed.
evidence: alternate.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, including VAT, both available immediately and with no crossed-out price: SanDisk Ultra USB Type-C 128 GB EUR 30.49, ADATA UC300 128 GB EUR 21.79. SanDisk's own product page confirms the 128 GB Type-C model.
differences: SanDisk states read up to 150 MB/s, against up to 100 MB/s for ADATA, so the brand is faster on paper. Neither alternate page lists a write speed or warranty. Shipping starts at EUR 7.99. No test we read covers these two.
why: If you mostly carry files between a phone and a laptop, you pay about 29% less for the same capacity and plug. If read speed matters to you, SanDisk's figure is higher.

title: SanDisk Ultra 128 GB microSD vs Kingston Canvas Select Plus 128 GB

alternative.product: Kingston Canvas Select Plus microSDXC, 128 GB (SDCS3/128GBSP)

summary: Both are 128 GB microSDXC cards rated Class 10, U1 and A1, and the Kingston costs about 15% less at alternate.
evidence: alternate.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, including VAT, both available immediately and with no crossed-out price: SanDisk Ultra EUR 32.09, Kingston Canvas Select Plus EUR 27.29. Both list Class 10, UHS-I U1 and A1. The SD Association page sets out that the speed symbols with a number show a minimum write speed.
differences: SanDisk's price includes an SD adapter. The Kingston page doesn't list one, so check if you need it. Kingston states read up to 150 MB/s and adds a V10 rating, against up to 140 MB/s for SanDisk. SanDisk lists write up to 10 MB/s. Kingston lists no write speed. No test we read covers these two.
why: The speed ratings on the labels match or lean to the Kingston, for a modest saving. The adapter is the one thing to check.

title: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB Twin Pack vs Kingston DataTraveler Exodia S 64 GB Twin Pack

brand.product: SanDisk Ultra USB 3.0 Flash Drive 64 GB, pack of 2

alternative.product: Kingston DataTraveler Exodia S USB 3.2 64 GB, twin pack

summary: Both are pairs of 64 GB USB sticks at 7dayshop on USB 3.0 or its later name, USB 3.2 Gen 1, and the Kingston twin pack costs about 54% less.
evidence: 7dayshop.com product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, including VAT, both in stock: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB pack of 2 at GBP 36.99 (shown down from GBP 39.99), Kingston DataTraveler Exodia S 64 GB twin pack at GBP 16.99. Alternate's page for the same SanDisk model notes that USB 3.2 Gen 1 is the current name of USB 3.0.
differences: SanDisk's price is reduced, so the gap would be wider at GBP 39.99. SanDisk's title and specification say 130 MB/s and its description says 100 MB/s. The Kingston page states no speed, so it may be slower. No test we read covers these two.
why: The capacity and USB generation match, and even at SanDisk's reduced price the Kingston pack is less than half the cost. If you copy large files often, check speeds before buying.

title: Rexel No.56 Staples vs Viking 26/6 Staples
summary: Both are boxes of 5000 metal 26/6 staples, and Viking's costs about 36% less at the single-pack price.
evidence: Both prices read on viking-direct.co.uk on 6 to 7 November 2026, both excluding VAT, at the 1 to 2 pack tier: Rexel GBP 3.09, Viking GBP 1.99. Viking says its staples fit 26/6 or No.56 staplers. Rexel's details are confirmed on Viking's Irish site. The prices on this page include the 20% VAT we added to Viking's prices.
differences: At 5 packs, before VAT, Rexel falls to GBP 2.59 and Viking to GBP 1.59. Viking's page states up to 25 sheets and a jam-resistant design, and Rexel's states 20 sheets. Your stapler sets the real limit. No test we read compares jams.
why: Both are 26/6, and Viking's page says its staples fit 26/6 or No.56 staplers, so for the same count the main difference on the pages is the price.

title: Avery L7163 Address Labels vs Viking Multipurpose Labels

brand.product: Avery UltraGrip Address Labels L7163-100, 99.1 x 38.1 mm, 100 sheets of 14

key_ingredients.name: 99.1 x 38.1 mm, 14 per sheet, laser, white

alternative.product: Viking Multipurpose Labels, 99.1 x 38.1 mm, 100 sheets of 14

key_ingredients.name: 99.1 x 38.1 mm, 14 per sheet, laser, white

summary: Same label size, sheet layout and label count for laser printers, and Viking's pack costs about 61% less even with Avery on promotion.
evidence: Both prices read on viking-direct.co.uk on 6 to 7 November 2026, both excluding VAT: Avery L7163-100 GBP 32.99, marked as a Black Friday promo price, with no regular price shown. Viking GBP 12.99 at the 1 to 2 pack tier. Both pages give 99.1 x 38.1 mm, 14 labels per sheet, 100 sheets, for laser printers. Avery's details are confirmed on Viking's Irish site. The prices on this page include the 20% VAT we added to Viking's prices.
differences: Avery's price is a promotion and may rise, which would widen the gap. Avery lists UltraGrip and Quick-Peel sheets and says made in the UK. Both pages say FSC certified. No test we read compares how well they stick or feed through a printer.
why: The size, layout and printer type match. Try a pack on your own printer before a big mailing.

title: Navigator Universal A4 80 gsm vs Viking Everyday A4 80 gsm

brand.product: Navigator Universal A4 Printer Paper 80 gsm, 169 CIE, 500 sheets

alternative.product: Viking Everyday A4 Printer Paper 80 gsm, 150 CIE, 500 sheets

summary: Same size, weight, finish and sheet count, with Viking about 26% cheaper per ream and a lower whiteness.
evidence: Both prices read on viking-direct.co.uk on 6 to 7 November 2026, both excluding VAT, at the 1 to 4 pack tier: Navigator GBP 5.79, Viking GBP 4.29. Both pages give A4, 80 gsm, smooth, 500 sheets. Navigator's details are confirmed on Viking's Irish site. The prices on this page include the 20% VAT we added to Viking's prices.
differences: Navigator is whiter, at 169 CIE. Viking's title says 150 CIE and its specification says 153 CIE. Bulk tiers reduce both prices. No test we read compares jams or print quality.
why: For drafts, invoices and letters the size and weight match, and a difference of about GBP 1.80 a ream adds up. Choose Navigator if you need a whiter sheet for reports or colour work.
